why: Every claimed resolution is a whole-problem claim of a landmark result, and none has had any expert uptake. The Clay page, Fortnow (June 2026) and a September 2026 tracker all still treat the problem as open. Each claim also carries several F10 signals: self-deposit servers, many patch revisions, self-contradicting authors, or unfaithfulness risks in Lean that nobody has examined. So all are not_credible, apart from the two claims that have specific identified flaws (Xu–Zhou and Deolalikar), which are knocked_down. The close call was Arthanari, an established polytope researcher. I set the claim aside because the author themself presents it as unrefereed and awaiting vetting, nobody took it up, and an earlier membership condition of theirs was shown insufficient. Williams, Fang et al. and OpenAI's permanent bounds concern different questions, so they are variant. Critiques and clarifications are none. The OpenAI entry has an empty systems list, so its AI role is none. Dong 2023 credits GPT-4 with the argument (generated), but it falls before the snapshot and is not credible.
doubts: The Arthanari events could be argued as doubtful rather than not_credible, since the author is an established researcher. Whether the Allender–Williams comment is a digested verification is moot, because it has scope none. The researcher did not establish whether IPI Letters (Vega) is refereed.
